title: KV-cache keyspace collision triggered A/B quality drift — investigation and safety runbook
creator: Anita Kumar
description: During a 5% A/B traffic experiment that routed to model-v2 (baseline model-v1 at 95%), we observed a gradual quality regression affecting ~2.8% of end-user sessions over a 4 hour window. Root cause analysis shows a non-obvious KV-cache keyspace collision between model variants when the serving runtime reused a normalized cache key that did not include the model variant identifier under high batching conditions. The collision caused stale cross-variant prefix reuse and introduced subtle tokenization/context misalignment for a subset of sequences, which manifested as reduced reranking scores and user-visible hallucinations in the downstream reranker. Automatic rollback did not fire because latency and error-rate SLOs remained within thresholds; only quality metrics moved, and they were not wired into the abort heuristic.
incident_summary: A/B test quality drift caused by KV-cache key collision across model variants. No large spike in latency or errors, so time-based rollback heuristics didn't trigger. Mitigation required cache fixes, telemetry expansion, and runbook updates to include quality-aware aborts.

steps_to_reproduce: 1) Run shadow replay harness with mixed requests that exercise prefix caching and KV-cache hits (use seeds from incident cohort)
2) Configure two model variants served from same runtime instance with aggressive continuous batching enabled
3) Observe that cache key generation path for prefix caching normalizes inputs but omits model variant id in the key under certain optimization flags
4) Trigger high-concurrency batching to increase probability of key collisions and compare token-level logits/reranker scores between isolated caches and the shared-cache scenario
remediation: 1) Code: change KV-cache key generation to include explicit model variant id and rollout id; add unit tests asserting key uniqueness across variants
2) Deployment: perform rolling update to runtime image with new keying behavior; invalidate or rotate affected cache partitions during rollout
3) Telemetry: add per-variant quality metrics (NDCG, response CLARITY score) to canary dashboards and create alert rules for relative quality delta > 5% over 1 hour
4) Safety: implement automated A/B abort that evaluates quality signals (not only latency/errors) and will progressively cut traffic if quality delta exceeds threshold for configured cohorts
5) Test: expand synthetic traffic suite to include cross-variant collision scenarios and nightly chaos tests that simulate shared-cache collisions

postmortem_summary: Root cause: shared KV-cache keying omitted model variant id when continuous batching optimizations applied, allowing cross-variant prefix reuse and stale context. Impact: quality regression in a small but measurable subset of queries during A/B experiment. Key fixes: variant-aware cache keys, telemetry for quality signals, and an automated A/B abort that considers quality deltas. Runbook updated to include these checks and to prescribe immediate cache partition flush + rollback when quality thresholds are breached. Actions assigned with owners and due dates; plan to include collision scenarios in nightly regression and chaos tests.
